mbpp_0159.reference_description: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print the season for the given month and day.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines SeasonFinder.monthSeason(month, days) which returns a season (winter, spring, summer, autumn) for a given month and day. It first selects a season based on the month, then refines it with day-based thresholds near equinoxes/solstices (e.g., March >19, June >20, September >21, December >20), effectively modeling seasonal boundaries.

mbpp_0189.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first missing positive number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: In-place First Missing Positive
Main goal: Find the smallest positive integer not present in the input array in O(n) time and O(1) extra space by normalizing out-of-range values, using the array itself as a presence marker (via increments by n), and then scanning for the first unmarked position; if all 1..n exist, return n+1.

mbpp_0771.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given expression is balanced or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ExpressionChecker – Balanced Brackets Validator
Main goal: Determine if a given string has properly balanced and nested pairs of (), {}, and [] using a stack; return true only if every opening bracket is matched by a corresponding closing bracket in the correct order and the string length is even. The algorithm pushes opening brackets, checks closing brackets by popping and validating the match, and ensures the stack is empty at the end (rejecting odd lengths, underflow, or mismatches).

mbpp_0323.reference_description: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to re-arrange the given array in alternating positive and negative items.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: In-place sign-alternating reordering via right rotation
Main goal: Rearrange an integer array in place so that non-negative numbers appear at even indices (0, 2, ...) and negative numbers at odd indices (1, 3, ...). It finds the first out-of-place index and, when it encounters a later element with the opposite sign, rotates the subarray to bring that element into the out-of-place position, updating the next target index accordingly. Zero is treated as non-negative.

mbpp_0522.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest bitonic subsequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
The code computes the length of the longest bitonic subsequence (increasing then decreasing) in the given array. It uses dynamic programming to build:
- lis[i]: the length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at index i
- lds[i]: the length of the longest decreasing subsequence starting at index i
Then it combines them as lis[i] + lds[i] - 1 for all i to obtain the maximum bitonic subsequence length.

mbpp_0776.reference_description: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count those characters which have vowels as their neighbors in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Consonant-vowel adjacency counter
Main goal: For a given string, count the number of consonant characters that are adjacent to at least one lowercase vowel (a, e, i, o, u). It checks inner positions and edge positions, ignores vowels, and returns the total count.

mbpp_0245.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of bi-tonic sub-sequence for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
The code computes the maximum sum of a bitonic subsequence (increasing then decreasing) in the given array. It builds:
- MSIBS[i]: maximum sum of an increasing subsequence that ends at index i.
- MSDBS[i]: maximum sum of a decreasing subsequence that starts at index i.
It then combines these at each peak i as MSIBS[i] + MSDBS[i] − arr[i] (to avoid double-counting the peak), and returns the maximum such value.

mbpp_0039.reference_description: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the letters of a given string can be rearranged so that two characters that are adjacent to each other are different.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Rearranges characters of string S so that no two adjacent characters are the same, using a max-heap (priority queue) of character counts. It counts frequencies, builds a heap, checks feasibility (if one character occurs more than (n+1)/2, returns an empty string). Then repeatedly takes the two most frequent characters, appends them, decrements counts, and reinserts if still positive, finally appending any remaining character. Returns the rearranged string or "" if impossible.

mbpp_0123.reference_description: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum all amicable numbers from 1 to a specified number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Amicable Numbers Sum Calculator
Main goal: Given a limit, identify amicable pairs (a, b) where the sum of proper divisors of a equals b and the sum of proper divisors of b equals a (with a ≠ b), collect each number once using a set, and return the sum of all amicable numbers found.

mbpp_0069.reference_description: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether array contains the given sublist or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SublistChecker - Contiguous sublist check
Main goal: Implement isSublist(l, s) to determine whether s appears as a contiguous subsequence inside l (empty s is always a sublist; if s equals l -> true; if s is longer than l -> false). It scans l and compares elements with s using equals.

mbpp_0515.reference_description: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if there is a subset with sum divisible by m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Subset Sum Modulo m DP

Goal: Check whether there exists a non-empty subset of the input array whose sum is divisible by m. It uses a dynamic programming array DP[r] (r in 0..m-1) to indicate whether some subset achieves remainder r modulo m, updates reachable residues with each element, and returns true if residue 0 becomes reachable. It also short-circuits with true when n > m (by a pigeonhole principle).

mbpp_0223.reference_description: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check for majority element in the given sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Determine whether x is the majority element (appears more than n/2 times) in the first n elements of a sorted array arr.

How it works:
- binarySearch finds the index of the first occurrence of x (or -1 if not found) using a binary search that ensures the found index is the first x in the array.
- isMajority uses binarySearch to locate the first x. If not found, returns false. If found at index i, it checks whether i + n/2 is within bounds and arr[i + n/2] is also x; if so, x appears at least n/2 + 1 times among the first n elements, so it returns true; otherwise false.

Assumptions: arr is sorted non-decreasing.

mbpp_0838.reference_description: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find minimum number swaps required to make two binary strings equal.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum swaps to make two binary strings equal
Main goal: Given two equal-length binary strings s1 and s2, compute the minimum number of swaps needed to make the strings identical; return -1 if impossible.
How it works: It counts mismatches where s1 has 0 and s2 has 1 (c0) and where s1 has 1 and s2 has 0 (c1). It computes base = c0/2 + c1/2. If both c0 and c1 are even, it returns base. If the total mismatches c0+c1 is even (i.e., both are odd), it returns base + 2. If the total mismatches is odd, it returns -1.

mbpp_0747.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LCS3 - Longest Common Subsequence of Three Strings
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest sequence common to three input strings X, Y, and Z using a 3D dynamic programming table. It fills L[i][j][k] with the recurrence: if any index is 0, L=0; if X[i-1], Y[j-1], and Z[k-1] match, L[i][j][k] = L[i-1][j-1][k-1]+1; otherwise L[i][j][k] = max(L[i-1][j][k], L[i][j-1][k], L[i][j][k-1]). Returns L[m][n][o], the length of the LCS among the three strings.

mbpp_0423.reference_description: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to solve gold mine problem.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes the maximum amount of gold that can be collected from an m×n grid when starting from any row in the first column and moving rightward. It uses dynamic programming: it fills a DP table goldTable by iterating columns from right to left and, for each cell, adding the cell's gold to the maximum of the three possible moves to the next column (right, right-up, right-down; boundaries yield 0). After filling, it returns the maximum value found in the first column of the DP table, representing the best starting row.

mbpp_0408.reference_description: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find k number of pairs which consist of one element from the first array and one element from the second array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: K Smallest Pairs Using a Min-Heap Frontier
Main goal: Given two sorted arrays nums1 and nums2 and an integer k, return up to k pairs [nums1[i], nums2[j]] with the smallest sums nums1[i] + nums2[j]. The code validates inputs, uses a min-heap ordered by the sum, starts from (0,0), and repeatedly pops the smallest pair, adds it to the result, and pushes its right neighbor (i, j+1) and, when on the first column (j == 0), its down neighbor (i+1, j). It stops when k pairs have been produced or the queue is empty. Assumes the input arrays are sorted to ensure correctness.

mbpp_0940.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using heap sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Heap Sort Implementation
Main goal: Sort an int[] in ascending order by building a max-heap (heapify) and repeatedly swapping the max element to the end and restoring the heap (shiftDown) to yield a sorted array in-place.

mbpp_0387.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the hexadecimal number is even or odd.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Determines if a hexadecimal number (provided as a string N) is even or odd by inspecting its least significant hex digit. The method evenOrOdd(String N) returns "Even" if the last character is 0, 2, 4, 6, A, C, or E, and "Odd" otherwise. It assumes a non-empty string with uppercase hex digits and does not handle lowercase or invalid input.

mbpp_0628.reference_description: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to replace all spaces in the given string with character * array item * array item * array item * array item '%20'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: URL-encoding of spaces in a string (replace spaces with %20)
Main goal: Trim the input, count spaces to determine the final length after replacing each space with "%20", return "-1" if that length exceeds 1000; otherwise build a new string by filling a char array from the end, replacing spaces with "%20" and copying other characters, producing a string where all spaces are replaced with "%20".

mbpp_0315.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first maximum length of even word.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Even-Length Word Finder
Main goal: Given a space-separated string, the code finds the longest word whose length is even and returns that word. It scans characters, counts the length of the current word, updates the best result when it encounters a space (or end of string) if the word length is even and greater than any previously found. If no even-length word exists, it returns "-1".

mbpp_0901.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest multiple of the first n numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SmallestMultiple - Least common multiple of the upper half of 1..n
Main goal: For a given n > 2, return the smallest positive number that is divisible by every integer from floor(n/2) + 1 up to n. It does this by starting with i = 2n and repeatedly increasing i by n until i is divisible by all integers in that range; n <= 2 is handled by returning n.

mbpp_0152.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using merge sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: MergeSort - Recursive merge sort implementation in Java. Main goal: sort an array of integers by recursively dividing it into halves and merging the sorted halves. The merge function merges two sorted int arrays into one sorted array, and the mergeSort function handles base cases, splits the input into left and right halves, recursively sorts them, and merges the results.

mbpp_0516.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using radix sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LSD Radix Sort (base 10) for non-negative integers

Main goal: Sort an int[] in ascending order by repeatedly bucketing numbers into 10 buckets based on the current digit (least significant first), flattening the buckets back into the array, and moving to the next higher digit until all digits of the maximum value have been processed.

mbpp_0834.reference_description: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to generate a square matrix filled with elements from 1 to n raised to the power of 2 in spiral order.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Creates an n-by-n matrix filled with numbers 1 through n^2 in clockwise spiral order, returning an empty matrix for n <= 0. It uses four boundaries (rowStart, rowEnd, colStart, colEnd) to iteratively fill the top row, right column, bottom row, and left column.

mbpp_0665.reference_description: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to shift first element to the end of given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Moves all copies of the first element to the end while preserving the order of other elements; if input is null or empty, returns an empty list.

mbpp_0938.reference_description: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find three closest elements from three sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds a triple (one element from each of three sorted arrays A, B, and C) such that the range (max - min) among the three chosen values is minimized. It uses a three-pointer approach (i, j, k) to walk the arrays, always advancing the pointer at the current minimum value and updating the best triple when a smaller range is found; it stops early if the range becomes zero. Returns the actual elements [A[resI], B[resJ], C[resK]].

mbpp_0898.reference_description: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract specified number of elements from a given array, which follow each other continuously.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Extractor.extractElements. Main goal: Identify and return the values that occur in exactly n consecutive equal numbers in the provided list (tracking runs of identical elements and adding the value when a run length equals n). The method handles null/empty inputs or non-positive n and considers the final run after iteration; duplicates may appear if the same value forms multiple qualifying runs.

mbpp_0501.reference_description: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find common divisor between two numbers in a given pair.

It first computes gcd(x, y) by brute-forcing from 1 to min(x, y) in ngcd, then counts the divisors of that gcd in numCommDiv by iterating up to sqrt(gcd) and counting factor pairs (adjusting for a possible square root divisor).

mbpp_0060.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum length of the subsequence with difference between adjacent elements for the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

mbpp_0822.reference_description: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to return true if the password is valid.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: PasswordValidator - Main goal: Validate a password against specific rules. The passValidity method returns true if the input string length is between 6 and 12, contains at least one lowercase letter, at least one digit, at least one uppercase letter, at least one of the characters $, #, or @, and contains no whitespace; otherwise it returns false.

mbpp_0548.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest increasing subsequence of the given sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Length (Dynamic Programming)
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence in the given integer array. It uses dynamic programming: lis[i] stores the length of the LIS ending at index i, initializes to 1, updates lis[i] when arr[i] > arr[j] and lis[i] < lis[j] + 1 for all j < i, and returns the maximum value among lis.

mbpp_0149.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest subsequence such that the difference between adjacents is one for the given array.

It uses dynamic programming: dp[i] stores the length of the longest valid subsequence ending at index i. For each i, it checks all j < i, and if arr[i] == arr[j] ± 1, updates dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1). Returns the maximum dp[i]. Time complexity is O(n^2), space O(n).

mbpp_0524.reference_description: Write a function to find the sum of maximum increasing subsequence of the given array.

It maintains msis[i] as the best sum of an increasing subsequence ending at index i (initialized to arr[i]), updates it by checking all previous j where arr[i] > arr[j], and finally returns the maximum value found in msis.

mbpp_0523.reference_description: Write a function to check whether a given string has a capital letter, a lower case letter, a number and specified length using lambda function.

mbpp_0468.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product formed by multiplying numbers of an increasing subsequence of that array.

It returns the maximum value across all mpis. Time complexity: O(n^2), Space: O(n).

mbpp_0926.reference_description: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n-th rencontres number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
The code implements Rencontres numbers. It counts permutations of n elements with exactly m fixed points. It includes:
- binomialCoeff(n,k): a simple recursive computation of C(n,k) with base cases k=0 or k=n.
- rencontresNumber(n,m): returns the number of permutations with exactly m fixed points, using D(n,m) = C(n,m) * D(n-m,0). It defines base cases for derangements: D(0,0)=1 and D(1,0)=0, and D(n,0) = (n-1)[D(n-1,0) + D(n-2,0)]. Potential issues: no guard for m>n and the binomial recursion is inefficient and may overflow for large n.

mbpp_0463.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum product subarray of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Maximum Product Subarray Calculator
Goal: This code tries to compute the maximum product of any contiguous subarray within the given integer array.

How it works (brief):
- It tracks two running values: maxEndingHere and minEndingHere, representing the maximum and minimum product for subarrays ending at the current position (needed to handle negative numbers).
- For each element:
  - If positive: multiply maxEndingHere by the element; update minEndingHere with the smaller of (minEndingHere * element) and 1.
  - If zero: reset both endings to 1.
  - If negative: swap roles using a temporary variable to compute new maxEndingHere and minEndingHere.
- It updates maxSoFar with the best maxEndingHere found.
- At the end, returns maxSoFar unless no positive product is possible (in which case it may return 0).

Caveat:
- There are edge cases (e.g., a single negative element like [-2]) where the true maximum product is negative, but the code can return 1, indicating a potential correctness issue for all-negative inputs. Overall, it’s intended as a O(n) solution using a dynamic programming style approach.

mbpp_0854.reference_description: Write a function which accepts an arbitrary array and converts it to a heap using heap queue algorithm.

mbpp_0113.reference_description: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a string represents an integer or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Determine if a trimmed string is a valid signed integer; accepts an optional leading + or -, requires digits thereafter, and returns true for valid, false for invalid, or null if the input is empty.

mbpp_0129.reference_description: Write a function to calculate magic square.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate magic square.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether a 2D int array is a magic square by summing all rows, all columns, and the two diagonals, then verifying that all these sums are equal. It collects these sums in a list and returns true if the set of sums has size 1. Note: the anti-diagonal is computed incorrectly (it uses [i][i] instead of [i][n-1-i]), so the check may not correctly verify the anti-diagonal.

mbpp_0469.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum profit earned from a maximum of k stock transactions
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming solution for Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
Main goal: Given an array of prices and an integer k, compute the maximum profit achievable with at most k buy-sell transactions. It uses a DP table finalProfit[i][j] representing the maximum profit with at most i transactions up to day j, and returns finalProfit[k][n-1]. Time complexity is O(k * n^2) and space complexity is O(k * n).

mbpp_0639.reference_description: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sum the length of the names of a given array of names after removing the names that start with a lowercase letter.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Calculate total length of properly capitalized names. Main goal: Iterate over a list of strings and, for each string with length > 1 that starts with an uppercase letter, verify that all remaining characters are lowercase; if so, add its length to a running total and return the total.

mbpp_0247.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest palindromic subsequence in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Determines the length of the longest palindromic subsequence (LPS) of a string using bottom-up dynamic programming. It fills a 2D DP table where L[i][j] stores the LPS length for substring str[i..j], initializes single-character substrings to 1, and uses end-character matches or mismatches to build up the solution, finally returning L[0][n-1].

mbpp_0382.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of rotations in a circularly sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Rotation count finder for a rotated sorted array
Main goal: Locate the index of the smallest element (the rotation pivot) in a rotated sorted array using a binary search algorithm, returning 0 if the array is already sorted (no rotation). The approach uses circular indexing (modulo) and runs in O(log n).

mbpp_0306.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of increasing subsequence from prefix till ith index and also including a given kth element which is after i, i.e., k > i .
Description_Simple.comparison_text: 2D dynamic programming approach for Maximum Sum Increasing Subsequence (MSIS). Goal: compute the maximum sum of an increasing subsequence from the input array using a two-dimensional DP table and return the value at dp[index][k]. The code initializes a base row with sums involving a[0], then fills a dp[i][j] table by considering extending subsequences when a[j] > a[i] and j > i, or carrying forward the best previous sums. The final result is taken from dp[index][k].

mbpp_0239.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of possible sequences of length n such that each of the next element is greater than or equal to twice of the previous element but less than or equal to m.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming Sequence Counter
Main goal: Compute the number of sequences of length n with a constraint m using a bottom-up DP table. The 2D array T[i][j] counts valid sequences with parameter i (a value bound) and length j. Rules:
- If i == 0 or j == 0: T[i][j] = 0
- If i < j: T[i][j] = 0
- If j == 1: T[i][j] = i (there are i single-element sequences)
- Otherwise: T[i][j] = T[i - 1][j] + T[i / 2][j - 1] (sum of two subproblems: sequences with max i-1 of length j and sequences of length j-1 with max floor(i/2))
The function returns T[m][n], the total number of sequences under these rules.

mbpp_0689.reference_description: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block

Description_Simple.reference_text: ## write a function to find the minimum number of jumps to reach the end of the array for the given array of integers where each element represents the max number of steps that can be made forward from that element. > indented block > indented block
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MinJumps - Minimum jumps to reach end
Main goal: Compute the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index of an array where each element represents the maximum jump length from that position, using a dynamic programming approach that fills a jumps[] array and returns Integer.MAX_VALUE if unreachable.

mbpp_0107.reference_description: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count hexadecimal numbers for a given range.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counts the total number of hexadecimal digits that are A–F (i.e., values 10–15) among all integers in the inclusive range [L, R]. For each i in [L, R], if 10 ≤ i ≤ 15 it adds 1; if i > 15, it examines each hex digit (via k % 16 and k /= 16) and adds 1 for every digit that is >= 10. Returns the sum of these counts.

mbpp_0466.reference_description: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the peak element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Peak Element Finder (Binary Search Style)
Main goal: Locate the index of a peak element in an array using a divide-and-conquer approach (binary search). A peak is an element not smaller than its neighbors, with proper handling at the boundaries.
Functions:
- findPeakUtil(arr, low, high, n): recursively checks the middle element and, if not a peak, recurses toward the side with a larger neighbor.
- findPeak(arr, n): wrapper that initiates the search over the entire array.
Complexity: O(log n) time, O(log n) auxiliary space due to recursion.

mbpp_0826.reference_description: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the type of triangle from the given sides.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: TriangleType; Main goal: determine if a triangle with sides a, b, c is right-, obtuse-, or acute-angled by comparing squared side lengths; note the right-angle check is incorrect (it uses sqa == sqa + sqb, etc.), so right-angle identification will fail in practice.

mbpp_0885.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the two given strings are isomorphic to each other or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Isomorphic Strings Checker
Main goal: Determine whether two strings are isomorphic by mapping each character to the list of its positions, then sorting and comparing these position lists to verify that the two strings share the same structural pattern.

mbpp_0108.reference_description: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to merge multiple sorted inputs into a single sorted iterator using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Merge three sorted lists using a min-heap
Goal: Merge three input integer lists into one sorted list. The code sorts each input list, then uses a PriorityQueue (min-heap) of Node objects (holding a value and its iterator) to repeatedly pull the smallest current value and advance that list, building the merged result.

mbpp_0121.reference_description: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the triplet with sum of the given array
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
- Title: Triplet Zero-Sum Finder
- Main goal: Determine whether there exists a subset of exactly three elements in the array A (with length n) whose sum is zero.
- How it works: checkTriplet(A, n, sum, count) is a recursive backtracking function that either includes the last element (n-1) by subtracting it from sum and incrementing count, or excludes it. It returns true when three elements have been chosen and their sum is zero (count == 3 && sum == 0); it returns false if three elements have been chosen without sum reaching zero, or if there are no elements left (n == 0), or if the remaining sum becomes negative (sum < 0).
- Initial call (implied): checkTriplet(A, A.length, 0, 0).
- Complexity note: Exponential worst-case time due to exploring subsets; effectively enumerates possible triplets.

mbpp_0570.reference_description: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove words from a given array of strings containing a character or string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RemoveWordsUtil - Filter words containing specified substrings

Main goal: Provide a utility method removeWords that, for each input line, splits the line into words and removes any word that contains any substring from a given list (charlist). It returns a new list of lines composed of the remaining words.

mbpp_0181.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common prefix in the given set of strings.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: Compute the longest common prefix (LCP) across the first n strings in an array. It provides two methods: commonPrefixUtil compares two strings character by character and returns their common prefix; commonPrefix initializes with the first string and iteratively shortens it by comparing with each subsequent string using commonPrefixUtil, resulting in the LCP of all n strings. Handles edge case n == 0 by returning an empty string.

mbpp_0485.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest palindromic number in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PalindromeUtils — Detect and locate the largest palindromic value in an integer array
Main goal: Provide a numeric palindrome checker (isPalindrome) that compares the leading and trailing digits without converting to a string, and a method (largestPalindrome) that sorts the input array and returns the largest element among the first n elements that is a palindrome, or -1 if none exist.

mbpp_0231.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum in the given right triangle of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: In-Place Dynamic Programming for Triangle Maximum Path Sum
Summary_description: The code computes the maximum possible sum from the top to the bottom of a triangle represented as a 2D array tri with n rows. It updates the triangle in place: it initializes the top two rows, then for each subsequent row updates the left and right edges by adding the value above, and for interior positions sets tri[i][j] to the maximum of the sums coming from the two possible parents (tri[i-1][j-1] and tri[i-1][j]). After processing all rows, it returns the maximum value in the last row, which corresponds to the maximum path sum from top to bottom. Time complexity is O(n^2) and it uses O(1) extra space (in-place).

mbpp_0397.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the median of three specific numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a MedianFinder class with a static method medianNumbers that returns the median (the middle value) of three integers a, b, and c by using nested conditional statements to determine which one lies between the other two.

mbpp_0685.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of prime numbers between 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of primes up to n using a sieve
Main goal: Compute and return the sum of all prime numbers <= n by implementing a basic Sieve of Eratosthenes. It initializes a boolean array of potential primes, marks multiples as non-prime, then sums all indices identified as prime.

mbpp_0526.reference_description: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to capitalize first and last letters of each word of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Returns a string where each word is transformed to have its first and last letters uppercased (the rest lowercased). It first lowercases the entire input, splits on whitespace, uppercases the first and last characters of each word (single-character words become that character), and rejoins words with single spaces. Null or empty input is returned unchanged.

mbpp_0863.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the longest sub-sequence such that elements in the subsequences are consecutive integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Consecutive Subsequence Length Calculator
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest set of consecutive integers present in the input array (duplicates ignored). The code sorts the array, builds a list of unique values, then scans to find the maximum run where consecutive elements differ by exactly 1, returning that length. Note: It assumes n > 0 and would fail for an empty input.

mbpp_0632.reference_description: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MoveZerosToEnd
Main goal: Create and return a new list where all non-zero elements keep their original order and all zeros are moved to the end; the input list is not modified.

mbpp_0971.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum number of segments of lengths a, b and c that can be formed from n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum number of segments by cutting a rod into lengths a, b, or c (dynamic programming)
Main goal: Given n and segment lengths a, b, c, compute the maximum number of pieces a rod of length n can be cut into using only pieces of those lengths. The function uses a 1D DP array dp where dp[i] stores the maximum number of pieces to achieve length i (initialized to -1, with dp[0] = 0). It updates dp[i+a], dp[i+b], and dp[i+c] for valid indices, and finally returns dp[n] (or -1 if impossible).

mbpp_0745.reference_description: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find numbers within a given range where every number is divisible by every digit it contains.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements a function divisibleByDigits that returns all numbers in the inclusive range [startnum, endnum] for which every decimal digit is non-zero and divides the number itself. It checks each number by inspecting its digits (via string conversion) and collects those that satisfy n % digit == 0 for every digit into a list, which is then returned.

mbpp_0943.reference_description: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to combine two given sorted arrays using heapq module.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Merges two sorted lists of integers into a new sorted list using a two-pointer approach, returning all elements in non-decreasing order without modifying the inputs (linear time, O(n+m) time and space).

mbpp_0256.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of prime numbers less than a given non-negative number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Java class PrimeCounter with method countPrimesNums(int n) counts how many prime numbers exist in [2, n-1] by a naive primality test (for each number from 2 up to n-1, checks divisibility by all integers from 2 to num-1); returns the total count. The approach uses straightforward trial division and has quadratic time complexity in the worst case.

mbpp_0054.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using counting sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Counting sort implementation for non-negative integers: it finds the maximum value, builds a frequency bucket array, counts occurrences of each value, and rewrites the input array in ascending order, returning the sorted array.

mbpp_0620.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest subset where each pair is divisible.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Longest Divisible-Adjacent Subsequence (Dynamic Programming)
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest subsequence of the input array where each consecutive pair satisfies a divisibility relation (a[i] divides a[j] or a[j] divides a[i]), using a bottom-up DP that runs in O(n^2) time and O(n) space.

mbpp_0597.reference_description: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find kth element from the given two sorted arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a method that merges two sorted arrays (arr1 of length m and arr2 of length n) into a new sorted array, then returns the k-th smallest element (1-based) from the merged result. It uses a standard two-pointer merge, handles any remaining elements, and yields the result at index k-1. Time complexity is O(m+n) and space complexity is O(m+n). Assumes 1 <= k <= m+n.

mbpp_0588.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the difference between largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes the range (maximum minus minimum) of the elements in a non-null, non-empty int array, throwing an exception for invalid input; it scans for min and max and returns their difference.

mbpp_0922.reference_description: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a pair with the highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Product Pair Finder
Main goal: Given an array of integers, find and return a pair of elements (x, y) whose product is the largest among all pairs, using a brute-force O(n^2) search. It handles null or short arrays by returning null, uses long for safe product comparison, and returns the first pair that achieves the maximum product in case of ties.

mbpp_0415.reference_description: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find a pair with highest product from a given array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxProduct
Main goal: Find and return the two elements in arr whose product is maximal by checking all unique pairs (O(n^2)); it validates input and throws if arr is null or has fewer than two elements.

mbpp_0476.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of the largest and smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of minimum and maximum in an array
Main goal: Validate input (non-null, non-empty); find the smallest and largest values in nums; return their sum (max + min); runs in O(n) time with O(1) extra space; throws IllegalArgumentException for invalid input.

mbpp_0751.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given array represents min heap or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: MinHeapChecker: Validate that an array-based binary heap satisfies the min-heap property by recursively checking that each node is less than or equal to its left and right children (when present) starting from a given index i.

mbpp_0531.reference_description: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find minimum number of coins that make a given value.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Minimum Coin Change (No DP)

Main goal: Compute the minimal number of coins needed to make value V from the given denominations using a brute-force recursive search. It returns 0 when V is 0; for each coin ≤ V it recurses on V − coin and takes the minimum subproblem result plus one; if no combination can form V it returns Integer.MAX_VALUE. The approach has no memoization, leading to exponential time.

mbpp_0918.reference_description: Write a function to count coin change.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count coin change.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Coin Change Dynamic Programming — Count ways to make amount n with given coin denominations

Main goal: Compute the number of combinations to form amount n using the first m coins from S, with unlimited supply.

Brief explanation: Uses a 2D DP array where table[i][j] is the number of ways to make amount i using the first j+1 coins. Initializes table[0][*] = 1, and fills with table[i][j] = table[i - S[j]][j] + table[i][j-1] (handling bounds). Returns table[n][m-1].

mbpp_0342.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest range that includes at-least one element from each of the given arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from k Sorted Lists
Main goal: Given k sorted lists, find the smallest numeric range [low, high] that contains at least one element from each list. It uses a min-heap (priority queue) of Node(value, listNum, index), initialized with the first element of every list, and tracks the current maximum value (high). Repeatedly pop the smallest value (low), update the best range if [low, high] is narrower, advance in the corresponding list by pushing its next element, and update high. The process ends when any list is exhausted, returning the best range found.

mbpp_0622.reference_description: Write a function to find the median of two sorted arrays of same size.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the median of two sorted arrays of same size.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The goal is to compute the median of two sorted arrays arr1 and arr2 (each of length n) using a two-pointer merge-like approach. It traverses the arrays to simulate merging, tracks the last two seen elements (m1 and m2), and returns their average as the median. Note: there is a bug when one array is exhausted—the code uses arr2[0] or arr1[0] instead of the current element (which can yield incorrect results).

mbpp_0448.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the sum of perrin numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PerrinSum - Sum of Perrin numbers up to n
Main goal: Compute the cumulative sum S = P0 + P1 + ... + Pn of Perrin numbers, with P0=3, P1=0, P2=2 and Pk = P(k-2) + P(k-3). The code handles base cases for n = 0, 1, 2, then iteratively generates P3..Pn and adds them to the total, returning the sum.

mbpp_0819.reference_description: Write a function to count the frequency of consecutive duplicate elements in a given array of numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the frequency of consecutive duplicate elements in a given array of numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Run-Length Encoding for Consecutive Duplicates
Main goal: Given a list of integers, produce two parallel lists representing runs of consecutive equal values: elements (the value at each run) and frequencies (the length of each run). It returns a Result containing these two lists; if the input is null or empty, it returns empty lists. The Result class exposes getters for both lists.

mbpp_0702.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of elements that should be removed such that amax-amin<=k.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum Removals to Ensure a Range of at Most k
Main goal: Compute the smallest number of elements to remove from an array so that the remaining elements have max - min ≤ k. It sorts the array, and for each starting index i, uses a binary search (findInd) to locate the furthest index j to the right such that arr[j] - arr[i] ≤ k. It then considers keeping the subarray [i, j] (length j - i + 1) and updates the minimum removals as n - (j - i + 1). The result is the minimal removals needed to satisfy the condition.

mbpp_0714.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of distinct power of prime factor of given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: countFac - triangular-exponent based prime-factor count

Main goal: Factorize the input n into its prime factors. For each prime factor with exponent e, add to a running total the largest k such that k(k+1)/2 ≤ e. After processing factors up to sqrt(original n), if a remaining prime factor remains, increment the count by 1. Return the final count.

mbpp_0141.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using pancake sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using pancake sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Pancake Sort Implementation
Main goal: Sort an integer array in ascending order in place using pancake sort by repeatedly flipping to bring the current maximum to the front and then to its correct position at the end of the unsorted portion.

mbpp_0853.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of odd factors of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Sum of odd divisors calculator

Main goal: Given a positive integer n, compute the sum of all its odd divisors (i.e., the sum of divisors of the odd part of n). The function strips out all factors of 2, then factors the remaining odd part and multiplies the geometric series (1 + p + p^2 + ... + p^a) for each odd prime factor p^a. If a leftover prime remains, it contributes (1 + n). Returns the product, which equals the sum of all odd divisors of the original n. Note: n = 0 is not handled (infinite loop risk).

mbpp_0717.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the standard deviation.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the standard deviation.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The Statistics class provides two helpers to compute basic statistics on an array of doubles. avgCalc returns the arithmetic mean of the elements (with a shortcut for a single-element array), and sdCalc computes the sample standard deviation by measuring squared deviations from the mean and dividing by (n-1). It returns 0.0 for arrays of length 0 or 1 when calculating SD. Note: avgCalc assumes the array is non-empty; with an empty array it would throw an exception.

mbpp_0071.reference_description: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array of elements using comb sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Java Comb Sort Implementation
Main goal: Sort an integer array in ascending order using Comb Sort with a shrink factor of 1.3; it repeatedly reduces the gap and swaps elements that are out of order, continuing until the array is sorted.

mbpp_0131.reference_description: Write a java function to reverse only the vowels of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to reverse only the vowels of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Reverse Vowels in a String. Main goal: return a new string where all vowels appear in reversed order relative to their original positions, while consonants stay in their original places. It collects vowels from the input, then rebuilds the string by inserting those vowels in reverse order.

mbpp_0122.reference_description: Write a function to find n’th smart number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find n’th smart number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Smart Number Finder
Main goal: Find the nth smallest integer less than MAX that has at least three distinct prime factors, using a sieve-like approach that marks primes and decrements a counter for each multiple of a prime; when a number’s counter reaches -3 it is collected, and after processing all numbers, the list is sorted and the nth element is returned.

mbpp_0374.reference_description: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print all permutations of a given string including duplicates.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: generate all unique permutations of a given string. The permuteString method recursively permutes the substring excluding the first character, then inserts the first character at every possible position in each of those permutations, collecting the results (avoiding duplicates). Base case: an empty string yields a list containing the empty string.

mbpp_0652.reference_description: Write a function to flatten the given tuple matrix into the tuple array with each tuple representing each column.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to flatten the given tuple matrix into the tuple array with each tuple representing each column.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Flatten and Transpose Nested Integer Tuples
Main goal: Take a List<List<int[]>>, flatten it into a single list of int[], then for each position i in the inner arrays, create an int[] consisting of the i-th elements from all flattened elements, collecting these into a List<int[]> and returning its string form. If input is empty, returns "[]"; assumes all inner int[] have the same length.

mbpp_0175.reference_description: Write a function to verify validity of a string of parentheses.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to verify validity of a string of parentheses.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Balanced Parentheses Validator
Main goal: Determine whether a string contains correctly balanced and properly nested pairs of (), {}, and [] by using a stack to push opening characters and a map to verify matching closing characters; returns true if balanced, false otherwise.

mbpp_0386.reference_description: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the minimum no of swaps required for bracket balancing in the given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Summary_description>Calculates the minimum number of adjacent swaps needed to balance a string consisting of '[' and ']'. It iterates the string, tracking counts of left and right brackets and an imbalance (unmatched ']').
When a '[' is encountered and there is a positive imbalance, it adds the current imbalance to the swap total and decreases the imbalance, effectively moving the '[' left past unmatched ']'. The function returns the total number of required swaps.

mbpp_0846.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum number of platforms required for a railway\/bus station.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Calculates the minimum number of platforms required at a train station for given arrival and departure times. It sorts the arrival and departure arrays and uses a two-pointer sweep to count overlapping intervals, updating the maximum number of simultaneously arriving trains (platforms) needed.

mbpp_0661.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum that can be formed which has no three consecutive elements present.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum that can be formed which has no three consecutive elements present.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
A dynamic programming solution that computes the maximum sum obtainable by choosing non-overlapping blocks of consecutive elements of length 1 or 2 from the array. It maintains an array sum[] where sum[i] stores the best total sum considering elements up to index i, using transitions:
- skip i (sum[i-1]),
- take i as a single element (sum[i-2] + arr[i]),
- take i and i-1 as a pair (sum[i-3] + arr[i] + arr[i-1]).
Base cases initialize sum[0], sum[1], and sum[2]; the final answer is sum[n-1].

mbpp_0829.reference_description: Write a function to find out the second most repeated (or frequent) string in the given sequence.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the second most repeated (or frequent) string in the given sequence.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SecondFrequentFinder - find the second most frequent string
Main goal: Given a list of strings, count occurrences, determine the second-highest frequency, and return a string with that frequency (or null if there are fewer than two distinct strings). Note: in case of ties for second place, the returned string depends on hashmap iteration order.

mbpp_0395.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first non-repeated character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: FirstNonRepeatingCharacter - Find the first non-repeating character in a string

Goal: Return the first character that appears exactly once in the given string; if none exist, return null. The code counts character frequencies with a HashMap and preserves the order of first appearances with a List. It first builds both structures in a single scan, then iterates the recorded order to return the first character with count 1.

mbpp_0001.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum cost path to reach (m, n) from (0, 0) for the given cost matrix cost[][] and a position (m, n) in cost[][].
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum Cost Path in a Grid
Main goal: Compute the minimum total cost to reach cell (m, n) from (0,0) in a matrix cost, where moves are right, down, or diagonal down-right, using dynamic programming.
How it works: It builds a DP table tc with tc[0][0] = cost[0][0], initializes the first row and first column, then fills the rest via tc[i][j] = min(tc[i-1][j-1], tc[i-1][j], tc[i][j-1]) + cost[i][j], and returns tc[m][n].

mbpp_0020.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given number is woodball or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines WoodallChecker with a method isWoodall(long x) that checks whether x is a Woodall number (x = n*2^n - 1 for some n). It immediately returns false for even x, true for x == 1, then computes x+1 and factors it as x+1 = 2^p * m by repeatedly dividing by 2. If at any division step the odd factor m equals p, it returns true; otherwise, after the loop, it returns false.

mbpp_0070.reference_description: Write a function to find whether all the given tuples have equal length or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find whether all the given tuples have equal length or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleUtils - Check uniform length of inner lists
Main goal: To verify whether all lists contained in a list of lists have the same length k and expose a human-readable result.
Functions:
- findEqualTuple(input, k): Returns 1 if every inner list has size k, otherwise returns 0.
- getEqual(input, k): Returns "All tuples have same length" if findEqualTuple == 1, else "All tuples do not have same length".
Notes:
- If input is empty, findEqualTuple returns 1 (treats as all having same length).

mbpp_0038.reference_description: Write a function to find the division of first even and odd number of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the division of first even and odd number of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Compute ratio of first even to first odd from a list
Main goal: Iterate the input list to find the first even number and the first odd number, then return the division of the firstEven by the firstOdd as a double. Note: If the list lacks an even or an odd, the method may produce incorrect results because it initializes the candidates to -1 and does not handle missing values.

mbpp_0492.reference_description: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to search an element in the given array by using binary search.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary Search for Existence in a Sorted Array
Main goal: Check if a given integer item exists in the sorted int[] itemList using binary search; returns true if found, otherwise false. It uses first/last boundaries, computes mid, and narrows the search range by comparing item with itemList[mid]. Time complexity: O(log n); assumes itemList is sorted in ascending order.

mbpp_0594.reference_description: Write a function to find the difference of first even and odd number of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the difference of first even and odd number of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DiffEvenOdd
Main goal: Return the difference between the first even and the first odd number found in a list (firstEven - firstOdd).

How it works:
- Scans the list to find the first even value (firstEven), defaulting to -1 if none is found.
- Scans the list again to find the first odd value (firstOdd), defaulting to -1 if none is found.
- Returns firstEven - firstOdd. If either parity is not present, the result uses -1 as a sentinel, which can lead to results like 0 or other values depending on which elements are missing.

Notes:
- Time complexity is O(n) due to two linear passes.
- Space complexity is O(1) beyond the input list.
- No handling for nulls or empty lists beyond the sentinel defaults.

mbpp_0496.reference_description: Write a function to find the smallest integers from a given array of numbers using heap queue algorithm.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the smallest integers from a given array of numbers using heap queue algorithm.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a method heapQueueSmallest that returns the n smallest numbers from a list. It uses a max-heap (priority queue with reverse order) of size n to keep the current n smallest values seen. It fills the heap with first n numbers, then for each subsequent number smaller than the heap’s maximum, it replaces the maximum. Finally it converts the heap to a list, sorts it ascending, and returns it. If n <= 0, it returns an empty list.

mbpp_0576.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether an array is subarray of another or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether an array is subarray of another or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether array B is a contiguous subarray of A. It uses two indices (i for A and j for B) and advances both when A[i] == B[j]. If j reaches m, it returns true. On a mismatch, it resets j to 0 and moves i forward to the next potential start with i = i - j + 1. If no match is found, it returns false. This is a naive substring-search approach (worst-case O(n*m)); note that with an empty B, it returns false under this implementation.

mbpp_0508.reference_description: Write a function to check if the common elements between two given arrays are in the same order or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the common elements between two given arrays are in the same order or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CommonOrder.sameOrder
Main goal: Determine if two lists contain the same sequence of elements that appear in both lists. It computes the intersection of elements, filters each list to only those elements (preserving order and duplicates), and then checks if the two filtered lists are equal.

mbpp_0032.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest prime factor of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the largest prime factor of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes and returns the largest prime factor of a given long integer n by performing trial division: it removes all factors of 2, then tests odd divisors up to sqrt(n), updating the maximum prime factor found, and finally returns n if the remaining value is greater than 2.

mbpp_0784.reference_description: Write a function to find the product of first even and odd number of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the product of first even and odd number of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds the first even and the first odd numbers in a list of integers (via two passes) and returns their product. If an even or an odd isn’t present, it uses -1 as a sentinel, which can yield unusual results (e.g., -1 * x, or 1 if neither exists). No null input handling.

mbpp_0810.reference_description: Write a function to iterate over elements repeating each as many times as its count.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to iterate over elements repeating each as many times as its count.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CounterUtil.countVariable — Generate a sequence from four counts

Main goal: Return a List<String> containing a occurrences of "p", followed by b occurrences of "q", followed by c occurrences of "r", and d occurrences of "s" (in that order). The method builds the list by iterating and appending each letter the specified number of times, using an ArrayList, and returns the result. If any count is zero or negative, the corresponding loop adds nothing.

mbpp_0684.reference_description: Write a java function to count occurences of a character in a repeated string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count occurences of a character in a repeated string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count occurrences of a character in the first 10 chars of a repeated string
Goal: For a given string str and character x, compute how many times x appears in the first 10 characters of the string formed by repeating str. The method counts x in the original str, scales by the number of full repetitions within length 10 (n / str.length()), then adds occurrences of x in the initial partial segment of str of length n % str.length(). It returns the total count. Note: if str.length() is 0, this will throw a division-by-zero error.

mbpp_0608.reference_description: Write a java function to find nth bell number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find nth bell number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Compute the nth Bell number using dynamic programming
Main goal: Calculate and return the nth Bell number (the number of partitions of an n-element set) by filling a 2D BigInteger table with the recurrence bell[i][j] = bell[i-1][j-1] + bell[i][j-1], initializing bell[0][0] = 1 and setting bell[i][0] = bell[i-1][i-1], finally returning bell[n][0].

mbpp_0428.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given array by using shell sort.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given array by using shell sort.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Shell sort for integers
Main goal: Sort an int[] in ascending order using Shell sort; begins with gap = n/2 and reduces gap by half each pass, performing insertion-sort-like shifting to insert each element.

mbpp_0158.reference_description: Write a java function to find k number of operations required to make all elements equal.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find k number of operations required to make all elements equal.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description:
Title: Equalize array elements by increments of k
Goal: Compute the minimum number of k-sized increments needed to raise every array element to the maximum value in the array; if any element's difference from the maximum is not a multiple of k, return -1.

mbpp_0781.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the count of divisors is even or odd.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the count of divisors is even or odd.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Divisor Parity Checker

Main goal: Given an integer n, determine whether the count of its positive divisors is even or odd, returning "Even" or "Odd".

How it works (brief): It attempts to count divisors by looping i from 1 up to floor(sqrt(n)) plus a small offset, adding 1 when i*i == n or 2 when i divides n (counting divisor pairs). It then returns "Even" if the total count is even, otherwise "Odd".

Note: The loop bound (i < (int)Math.sqrt(n) + 2) can lead to overcounting for non-squares, making some results unreliable, though mathematically a number has an odd divisor count only if it is a perfect square.

mbpp_0362.reference_description: Write a java function to find the item with maximum occurrences in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the item with maximum occurrences in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxOccurrences
Main goal: Return the element that occurs most frequently in a non-empty List<T> by counting frequencies for each item (using Collections.frequency). It validates input (throws IllegalArgumentException if null or empty) and, in case of ties, returns the first item encountered with the maximum frequency. Time complexity is O(n^2) due to repeated frequency calculations.

mbpp_0856.reference_description: Write a java function to find minimum adjacent swaps required to sort binary array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find minimum adjacent swaps required to sort binary array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Compute the minimum number of adjacent swaps required to move all 1s before all 0s by counting, for each 1, how many zeros lie to its right. It builds a suffix array of zero counts and sums these counts for every 1. Time complexity is O(n) and space complexity is O(n).

mbpp_0283.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the frequency of each digit is less than or equal to the digit itself.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the frequency of each digit is less than or equal to the digit itself.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Per-digit frequency validator
Main goal: Check that in the decimal representation of n, each digit i (0–9) occurs at most i times (which implies no zeros are allowed since i = 0). The method returns true if all per-digit constraints are satisfied, otherwise false. Note: there are edge-case quirks for n = 0 and negative numbers.

mbpp_0506.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the permutation coefficient of given p(n, k).
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Dynamic Programming computation of Stirling numbers of the second kind (S(n,k))

Main goal: Implement a DP to compute the number of ways to partition a set of n elements into k nonempty unlabeled subsets (the Stirling number of the second kind, S(n,k)) via permutationCoefficient(n, k).

What it does:
- Creates a 2D array P of size (n+1) x (k+1).
- Fills P using the recurrence P[i][j] = P[i-1][j] + j * P[i-1][j-1], which matches the standard recurrence S(i, j) = S(i-1, j) + j * S(i-1, j-1).
- Sets P[i][0] = 1 for all i (base case), and ensures P[i][j+1] is reset to 0 when building the table.
- Returns P[n][k] as a long.

Notes:
- The code intends to implement the Stirling numbers of the second kind, but the initialization P[i][0] = 1 for all i is incorrect for i > 0 (the correct base is S(i,0) = 0 for i > 0). This causes incorrect results for many (n, k) pairs.
- If corrected to standard bases (S(0,0)=1, S(i>0,0)=0, S(0,k>0)=0), the recurrence and structure would correctly compute S(n,k).
- Time and space complexity are O(n*k).

mbpp_0602.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first repeated character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first repeated character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Repeated Character Finder
Goal: Find the first character in the input string that repeats (appears at least twice) as you scan from left to right. The method checks each character by counting its occurrences in the prefix up to its position and returns the first character with a second occurrence. If no character repeats, it returns "None". Time complexity is O(n^2) due to the nested counting.

mbpp_0721.reference_description: Write a function to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths for the given square matrix of size n*n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find a path with the maximum average over all existing paths for the given square matrix of size n*n.
