mbpp_0869.reference_description: Write a function to remove sublists from a given array of arrays, which are outside a given range.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to remove sublists from a given array of arrays, which are outside a given range.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Filters a list of integer sublists by keeping only those whose elements all fall within the inclusive range [leftRange, rightRange]. For each (non-empty) sublist, it checks the minimum and maximum values; if min >= leftRange && max <= rightRange, the sublist is kept. Empty sublists are ignored. The method returns a new list containing references to the original sublists (no deep copies).

mbpp_0011.reference_description: Write a java function to remove first and last occurrence of a given character from the string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to remove first and last occurrence of a given character from the string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Remove the leftmost and rightmost occurrences of a character from a string
Main goal: The function removeOcc takes a string s and a character ch, removes the first occurrence of ch from the start, and then removes the last occurrence of ch from the end (on the updated string). Consequently, up to two occurrences of ch are removed (the leftmost and the rightmost in the original string). If fewer than two occurrences exist, it removes what is present. Returns the resulting string.

mbpp_0130.reference_description: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the item with maximum frequency in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Occurring Element Finder
Main goal: Given a List<T>, determine the element that appears most often and return it as a Map.Entry<T, Integer> (the element and its count). It builds a frequency map, then scans for the entry with the highest frequency.

mbpp_0232.reference_description: Write a function to get the n largest items from a dataset.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to get the n largest items from a dataset.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Top-N Largest Elements from a List
Main goal: Compute and return the n largest elements from a list of comparable items by using a min-heap (priority queue) of size n and outputting the results in descending order.

mbpp_0034.reference_description: Write a java function to find the missing number in a sorted array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the missing number in a sorted array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code uses binary search to locate the single missing number in a sorted array that should contain all integers from 1 to N except one. It assumes ar[i] should equal i+1 for a complete sequence. It returns -1 if no missing number is found (the array length is expected to be N-1).

mbpp_0029.reference_description: Write a java function to find the element occurring odd number of times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the element occurring odd number of times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Brute-force detector for the first odd-frequency element

Goal: The getOddOccurrence method searches the input array and returns the first element (by index) whose total frequency in the array is odd. It uses a nested loop to count occurrences of each element; as soon as it finds one with an odd count, it returns that value. If no element has an odd frequency, it returns -1. Time complexity is O(n^2) and space complexity is O(1). Note: if multiple values occur an odd number of times, the one with the smallest index in the array is returned.

mbpp_0304.reference_description: Write a java function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find element at a given index after number of rotations.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes the value at a given final index after applying a sequence of right-rotations on subarrays defined by ranges. After all ranges are processed, it returns arr[index], i.e., the element that ends up at the given final index.

mbpp_0604.reference_description: Write a function to reverse words in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to reverse words in a given string.

mbpp_0659.reference_description: Write a java function to print duplicants from array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to print duplicants from array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: DuplicateFinder.repeat – Detects distinct duplicates in an int array
Main goal: Given an int[] x, return a List<Integer> containing each distinct value that occurs at least twice in x. It uses a nested loop to compare all pairs and adds a value to the result only once (prevents duplicates in the output), resulting in O(n^2) time complexity.

mbpp_0207.reference_description: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the longest repeating subsequences such that the two subsequences don’t have same string characters at same positions.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Computes the length of the longest repeating subsequence in a given string using dynamic programming. It builds a (n+1) x (n+1) DP table where dp[i][j] stores the length of the longest repeating subsequence formed from the first i characters and the first j characters. If str.charAt(i-1) == str.charAt(j-1) and i != j, it extends the subsequence (dp[i][j] = 1 + dp[i-1][j-1]); otherwise it uses the maximum of the neighboring subproblems (dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j])). The result returned is dp[n][n]. The condition i != j ensures the two subsequences come from different positions in the string. Time and space complexity are O(n^2).

mbpp_0192.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether a string has atleast one letter and one number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether a string has atleast one letter and one number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: StringChecker.checkString; Main goal: Determine whether a given string contains at least one letter and at least one digit (returns true if both are present, false otherwise).

mbpp_0366.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest product of the pair of adjacent elements from a given array of integers.

mbpp_0275.reference_description: Write a java function to find the position of the last removed element from the given array.

mbpp_0842.reference_description: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number which occurs for odd number of times in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

mbpp_0510.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of subsequences having product smaller than k for the given non negative array.

mbpp_0188.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by product of two squares or not.

mbpp_0577.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last digit in factorial of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the last digit in factorial of a given number.

mbpp_0498.reference_description: Write a java function to find gcd of two positive integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find gcd of two positive integers.

Notes: assumes y != 0 and positive inputs; not robust for negative numbers or zero; time complexity is O(y).

mbpp_0183.reference_description: Write a function to count all the distinct pairs having a difference of k in any array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count all the distinct pairs having a difference of k in any array.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximize Sum of Valid Pairs in a Sorted Array
Main goal: Given an array, sort it and select non-overlapping adjacent pairs (in the sorted order) whose difference is strictly less than K to maximize the total sum of the selected elements.

Explanation:
- Sort the array.
- Use dynamic programming where dp[i] is the maximum sum achievable using elements up to index i.
- For each i from 1 to N-1, start with dp[i] = dp[i-1] (skip i). If arr[i] - arr[i-1] < K, consider forming a pair (i-1, i) with sum arr[i] + arr[i-1], adding it to dp[i-2] (or using pairSum directly if i == 1).
- The result is dp[N-1], i.e., the best total sum of non-overlapping valid pairs.

Complexity:
- Time: O(N log N) due to sorting, plus O(N) for DP.
- Space: O(N) for the dp array.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
<Summary_description>

Title: Simple min-jumps estimator for two jump lengths

Main goal: Provide a tiny, constant-time function to estimate the minimum number of jumps to reach distance d using two possible jump lengths a and b (after ordering so a <= b). It normalizes the inputs, then applies a few quick checks to return a jump count.

What the code does:
- Ensures a <= b by swapping if needed.
- If d >= b, returns the ceiling of d divided by b (i.e., using only jumps of length b).
- If d == 0, returns 0.
- If d == a, returns 1 (one jump of length a).
- Otherwise returns 2 (assumes at most two jumps suffice under this simplistic logic).

Note: This is a simplistic, case-based approach and does not solve the general minimum-jumps problem for arbitrary combinations of a, b, and d. It may be incorrect for many inputs where a combination of a and b is required to reach d exactly or with fewer than two jumps.

mbpp_0701.reference_description: Write a function to find the equilibrium index of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the equilibrium index of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: Equilibrium Index Finder. Main goal: Find the first index in the array where the sum of elements to the left equals the sum of elements to the right (the equilibrium index); returns -1 if none exist. Runs in linear time with constant extra space.

mbpp_0967.reference_description: Write a java function to accept the strings which contains all vowels.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to accept the strings which contains all vowels.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Vowel Coverage Checker — The code scans a string, collects distinct vowels (case-insensitive), and returns "accepted" only if all five vowels (a, e, i, o, u) appear; otherwise it returns "not accepted".

mbpp_0974.reference_description: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the minimum total path sum in the given triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum path sum in a triangle (dynamic programming)
Goal: Compute the smallest possible sum from the triangle's top to bottom by choosing adjacent numbers in each row. The code performs bottom-up DP: initialize memo with the bottom row, then for each upper row update memo[j] = row.get(j) + min(memo[j], memo[j+1]); return memo[0]. Time: O(n^2); Space: O(n).

mbpp_0102.reference_description: Write a function to convert snake case string to camel case string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert snake case string to camel case string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Snake_case to CamelCase Converter (PascalCase)
Main goal: Transform a snake_case string into a CamelCase (PascalCase) string by capitalizing the first letter of each underscore-delimited segment and lowercasing the rest, concatenating them, while preserving underscores that arise from empty segments (leading, trailing, or consecutive underscores).

mbpp_0134.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CheckLast
Main goal: Compute the sum of the first n elements of arr, then (if p == 1) return a parity label based on the sum (inverted: even sum -> "ODD", odd sum -> "EVEN"); if p != 1, always return "EVEN".

mbpp_0286.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous array in the modified array which is formed by repeating the given array k times.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum subarray sum for k repetitions
Main goal: Compute the maximum subarray sum for the array a repeated k times (i.e., concatenated k times) using Kadane’s algorithm. It loops over n*k elements, accessing a[i % n], keeps a running sum (maxEndingHere) and the best sum (maxSoFar), resets the running sum when it becomes negative, and initializes maxSoFar to handle all-negative cases.

mbpp_0311.reference_description: Write a java function to set the left most unset bit.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to set the left most unset bit.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The BitUtils.setLeftMostUnsetBit method returns a value obtained from n by turning on the least-significant zero bit within the bits up to the most-significant 1. If n is already of the form 2^k - 1 (all the lower bits are 1), it returns n unchanged. It finds the bit position of the rightmost 0 via a bit-scan and then returns n | (1 << pos).

mbpp_0411.reference_description: Write a function to convert the given snake case string to camel case string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert the given snake case string to camel case string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Snake to Camel (PascalCase) Converter
Main goal: Convert a snake_case string to a PascalCase (UpperCamel) string by capitalizing the first character of each non-empty segment and concatenating them; consecutive or edge underscores are preserved as underscores in the result.

mbpp_0355.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of rectangles in a circle of radius r.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: CountRectangles: Count lattice points inside a quarter-circle.

Main goal: For a given radius, count the number of positive integer pairs (a, b) with 1 ≤ a, b < 2*radius such that a^2 + b^2 ≤ (2*radius)^2, returning that count. This effectively counts axis-aligned rectangles with one corner at the origin whose opposite corner lies inside or on the circle of diameter 2*radius.

mbpp_0350.reference_description: Write a java function to minimize the length of the string by removing occurrence of only one character.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to minimize the length of the string by removing occurrence of only one character.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum deletions to make all characters equal
Main goal: For a given lowercase string s, compute the minimum number of deletions needed so that the remaining characters are all the same. It counts frequency of each letter 'a'–'z', finds the maximum frequency, and returns n - maxOcc. Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space (26-letter alphabet). Assumes only lowercase letters.

mbpp_0442.reference_description: Write a function to find the ration of positive numbers in an array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the ration of positive numbers in an array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: PositiveCounter – computes the ratio of positive integers in an input int array and returns that value as a double rounded to two decimals; returns 0.0 for an empty array.

mbpp_0530.reference_description: Write a function to find the ration of negative numbers in an array of integers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the ration of negative numbers in an array of integers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
NegativeRatio Calculator
Goal: Given an int[] nums, count how many elements are negative and return their ratio (negatives/length) as a double rounded to two decimal places; returns 0.0 for an empty array.

mbpp_0650.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given two arrays are equal or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Equality check for two integer arrays ignoring order
Main goal: Determine if two arrays contain exactly the same integers with the same multiplicities, regardless of their order. It sorts both arrays in place and compares corresponding elements, returning true only if all elements match. Note: It mutates inputs by sorting and has a bug in the comparison loop (it iterates only up to n-2, omitting the last element from the check).

mbpp_0575.reference_description: Write a java function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find nth number in a sequence which is not a multiple of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceCounter.countNo

Main goal: Given A, N, L, R, scan integers i from L to R and count how many are not divisible by A. The function returns the first i at which the count reaches N (or R if N is not reached within the range). It updates the result to the current i on each iteration and breaks once the non-multiple count equals N.

mbpp_0605.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given integer is a prime number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Goal: a method primeNum(int num) intended to check if a number is prime. However, its logic is flawed: it returns after the first non-divisor, misclassifying many numbers (e.g., it will label 2 or 3 incorrectly, and non-primes as primes). It also mishandles edge cases (numbers < 2) and stops early instead of testing all possible divisors up to sqrt(num). A correct version would test all divisors up to sqrt(num) and return true only after completing the loop, with num < 2 returning false.

mbpp_0047.reference_description: Write a java function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the last digit when factorial of a divides factorial of b.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Last-digit of product in (A, B]
Main goal: Compute the last decimal digit of the product of integers from A+1 to B. If A == B, return 1; if B - A >= 5, return 0 (the product ends with 0); otherwise multiply the last digits (i % 10) of each factor modulo 10 and return the result.

mbpp_0828.reference_description: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count alphabets,digits and special charactes in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Character type counter
Main goal: Given a string, count how many alphabetic characters, digits, and other (special) characters it contains, returning the results as an int array in the order [alphabets, digits, special].

mbpp_0657.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first digit in factorial of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a class FactorialFirstDigit with a method firstDigit(int n). It computes the leading (first) digit of n! by building the factorial using BigInteger, removing trailing zeros after each multiplication (dividing by 10 while divisible by 10) to avoid growth from factors of 10, and finally reducing the result to a single digit by repeatedly dividing by 10 until only the most significant digit remains, which is returned as an int.

mbpp_0757.reference_description: Write a function to count the pairs of reverse strings in the given string array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the pairs of reverse strings in the given string array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count reverse-string matches in a list
Main goal: Given a list of strings, count how many pairs (i, j) with i <= j satisfy testList[j] equals the reverse of testList[i], and return that count as a string. It uses a nested loop: for each element, compute its reverse and compare it against elements from the current index to the end. Palindromic strings contribute as self-matches. Time complexity is O(n^2) and space complexity is O(1) besides input storage.

mbpp_0357.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum element of all the given tuple records.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum element of all the given tuple records.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find the maximum integer in a nested list of numeric strings
Main goal: Iterate over a List<List<String>>, parse every string to an int, and return the largest value found. Initializes the result to Integer.MIN_VALUE and returns that if the outer list is empty. Potential NumberFormatException if any string is not a valid integer.

mbpp_0096.reference_description: Write a java function to find the number of divisors of a given integer.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the number of divisors of a given integer.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Divisor.divisor(n) computes the number of positive divisors of n
Main goal: Determine how many integers from 1 to n divide n (the divisor count d(n)). The code does this by counting divisors inside a nested loop; however, the outer loop repeats the same count n times unnecessarily, so the final result is still the divisor count, but with redundant computation (O(n^2) time). Negative or zero n yields 0 due to loop conditions.

mbpp_0351.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first element occurring k times in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First element with exactly k occurrences in a prefix of an array
Main goal: Find and return the first element in arr[0..n-1] that occurs exactly k times; if none exists, return -1. The code builds a frequency map of elements, then scans the array again to locate the first element whose count equals k.

mbpp_0225.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum element in a sorted and rotated array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find minimum in rotated sorted array with duplicates
Main goal: Return the smallest element in a rotated sorted array that may contain duplicates using a modified binary search on indices [low, high]. It compares mid to high to narrow the search range and finally returns arr[high] as the minimum.

mbpp_0384.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the smallest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code returns the count of how many times the smallest value appears in the given array arr of length n. It initializes the minimum with the first element and its frequency to 1, then scans the rest of the array: if a smaller value is found, it updates the minimum and resets the count to 1; if a value equals the current minimum, it increments the count. Finally, it returns the frequency of the smallest element (assuming n > 0).

mbpp_0505.reference_description: Write a function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to move all zeroes to the end of the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Moves all non-zero elements to the front of the input array in their original order, filling the remaining slots with zeros; modifies the array in place and returns it.

mbpp_0489.reference_description: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the frequency of the largest value in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Frequency of Largest Element in an Array
Goal: Return the count of occurrences of the maximum value in the array of size n by scanning once and updating the current maximum and its frequency (assuming a non-empty array).

mbpp_0414.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the value exists in a sequence or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the value exists in a sequence or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: OverlapChecker
Goal: Check if two lists share any common element. The overlapping(...) method returns 1 if any element from list1 equals any element from list2, otherwise returns 0. It uses a double loop with equals() to compare all pairs (O(n*m)). Note potential NullPointerExceptions if elements are null.

mbpp_0627.reference_description: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the smallest missing number from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Binary-search-based first-missing index finder in a 0-based array
Main goal: Return the smallest index i where array[i] != i, i.e., the first missing non-negative integer, assuming the array is organized so that all positions before the first missing value satisfy array[i] == i. It uses a recursive binary-search approach:
- If start > end, return end + 1 (no missing in the current range)
- If array[start] != start, return start (missing at the start)
- Let mid = (start + end) / 2; if array[mid] == mid, search the right half; else search the left half.
This finds the first index where the value diverges from its index in O(log n) time.

mbpp_0557.reference_description: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to toggle characters case in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Response:
Title: Toggle Case String Utility
Main goal: Invert the case of every alphabetic character in the input string (uppercase to lowercase and vice versa), while leaving non-letter characters unchanged; implemented by iterating over characters and building the result with a StringBuilder.

mbpp_0559.reference_description: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the largest sum of contiguous subarray in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxSubArray using Kadane's algorithm
Main goal: Determine the largest sum of any contiguous subarray of the input array, returning 0 if all elements are negative (i.e., allows the empty subarray). It uses a running sum (maxEndingHere) reset to zero when negative and tracks the best sum (maxSoFar).

mbpp_0546.reference_description: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the last occurrence of a character in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LastOccurrence - Find the last 1-based index of a character
Main goal: Return the 1-based position of the last occurrence of a specified character in the input string, or null if the character is not present.

mbpp_0681.reference_description: Write a java function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the smallest prime divisor of a number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Find the smallest divisor of a positive integer n (i.e., the smallest prime factor if n is composite, or n itself if n is prime).

How it works: 
- If n is even, return 2. 
- Otherwise, iterate over odd i starting at 3, checking i*i <= n (using a long cast to avoid overflow). If n % i == 0, return i. 
- If no divisor is found, return n (meaning n is prime). 
- Note: for n <= 1, the method returns n.

mbpp_0874.reference_description: Write a java function to check if the string is a concatenation of another string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check if the string is a concatenation of another string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Checks whether str1 is formed by repeating str2 (zero or more times). It returns true if n (length of str1) is a multiple of m (length of str2) and every character in str1 matches the corresponding character in str2 when str2 is cycled; otherwise false. Note: it fails for an empty str2 (division by zero) and an empty str1 is considered valid (0 repeats).

mbpp_0706.reference_description: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find whether an array is subset of another array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Subset Verification Between Two Arrays
Main goal: Determine if every element in arr2 (the first n elements) is present among the first m elements of arr1 by building a HashSet from arr1[0..m-1] and checking each arr2[i] for membership; returns true if all are present, false otherwise.

mbpp_0903.reference_description: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the total unset bits from 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: BitUtils.countUnsetBits — Total number of zero bits in the binary representations of all integers from 1 to n. The method loops i from 1 to n and, for each i, counts how many bits are 0 in its binary form by repeatedly dividing by 2 and incrementing the counter whenever the least significant bit is 0. Returns the sum. Note: if n <= 0, the result is 0.

mbpp_0025.reference_description: Write a java function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the product of non-repeated elements in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Product of distinct elements in an array
Main goal: Sort the array and return the product of each distinct value (effectively the product of all unique numbers, with a special case that if all elements are identical, the result is 1).

mbpp_0952.reference_description: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to compute the value of ncr mod p.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Efficient computation of nCr modulo p using 1D dynamic programming
Main goal: Compute C(n, r) modulo p by exploiting symmetry (r = min(r, n−r)) and updating a 1D array to iteratively build binomial coefficients, returning C[n][r] mod p. Time complexity is O(n · min(r, n−r)) and space complexity is O(min(r, n−r)).

mbpp_0026.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given tuple array has all k elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given tuple array has all k elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: All-elements-equal-to-K verifier
Main goal: Determine if every element in a List<List<Integer>> equals K; return true only if all elements are K, otherwise false. It iterates through all elements without early exit; empty input yields true. Note: potential null inputs may cause exceptions.

mbpp_0969.reference_description: Write a function to join the tuples if they have similar initial elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to join the tuples if they have similar initial elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Joins consecutive lists by grouping those with the same first element: it keeps the first element of the group and appends the remaining elements of subsequent lists (excluding their first element) to that group; otherwise it starts a new group.

mbpp_0125.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum difference between the number of 0s and number of 1s in any sub-string of the given binary string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum difference between the number of 0s and number of 1s in any sub-string of the given binary string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Finds the maximum subarray sum by treating '0' as +1 and '1' as -1 over the first n characters, i.e., the maximum (zeros − ones) in any contiguous substring of the string.

mbpp_0101.reference_description: Write a function to find the kth element in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the kth element in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Sorts the first n elements of the given array in ascending order using bubble sort, then returns the k-th smallest element (assuming k is 1-based). The method sorts in place and returns arr[k-1].

mbpp_0111.reference_description: Write a function to find common elements in given nested arrays. * array item * array item * array item * array item

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find common elements in given nested arrays. * array item * array item * array item * array item
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Goal: Return the elements that are present in every inner list of a list of lists.

What it does: A generic static method commonInNestedLists takes List<List<T>> and returns a List<T> containing elements common to all inner lists. If input is null or empty, it returns an empty list. It initializes a set with the first inner list’s elements and then intersects it with each subsequent inner list using retainAll. Finally, it converts the result set to a List and returns it. Note: duplicates are removed (due to the set) and order is not preserved (HashSet). Assumes inner lists are non-null.

mbpp_0142.reference_description: Write a function to count the same pair in three given arrays.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the same pair in three given arrays.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Three-list element-wise equality counter
Main goal: Return the number of indices i across three lists where list1[i], list2[i], and list3[i] are all equal (using equals), iterating up to the smallest of the three list sizes. The method is generic (type T) and relies on equals() for comparison; it may throw a NullPointerException if any compared element is null.

mbpp_0147.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum total path sum in the given triangle.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Bottom-Up In-Place DP for Triangle Maximum Path Sum
Goal: Compute the maximum total from top to bottom of a triangular array by updating each cell to the maximum sum obtainable from that cell to the bottom (in place), and return the top element tri[0][0].

mbpp_0343.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the number of digits and letters in a string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the number of digits and letters in a string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: digLet - count letters and digits
Goal: For a given string s, return an int[] where the first element is the count of letter characters and the second is the count of digit characters in s; all other characters are ignored.

mbpp_0187.reference_description: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given two sequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Longest Common Subsequence Length
Main goal: Compute the length of the longest common subsequence of two character arrays X and Y using a naive recursive approach. If either sequence length m or n is zero, return 0. If the last characters match (X[m-1] == Y[n-1]), increment the result by 1 and recurse on (m-1, n-1). Otherwise, return the maximum of the two recursive calls: (m, n-1) and (m-1, n). Note: runs in exponential time due to overlapping subproblems and lacks memoization/dynamic programming.

mbpp_0385.reference_description: Write a function to find the n'th perrin number using recursion.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the n'th perrin number using recursion.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Perrin sequence calculator (recursive)
Main goal: Provide a function to compute the nth Perrin number using the recurrence P(0)=3, P(1)=0, P(2)=2 and P(n)=P(n-2)+P(n-3) for n≥3 through a public static method getPerrin(int n) in class Perrin. Notes: uses simple recursion without memoization; returns int.

mbpp_0867.reference_description: Write a java function to add a minimum number such that the sum of array becomes even.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to add a minimum number such that the sum of array becomes even.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Parity-based result from count of odd elements
Main goal: Count how many odd numbers exist among the first n elements of arr and return 1 if that count is odd; otherwise return 2.
How it works: Iterates i from 0 to n-1, increments odd when arr[i] is odd, then returns 1 if odd is odd, else returns 2.

mbpp_0635.reference_description: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to push all values into a heap and then pop off the smallest values one at a time.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: HeapSort via PriorityQueue
Main goal: Convert a collection of comparable elements into a sorted list by inserting all items into a min-heap (PriorityQueue) and polling elements to produce an ascending-ordered List. It uses a generic type T that extends Comparable.

mbpp_0831.reference_description: Write a java function to count equal element pairs from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count equal element pairs from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PairCounter
Goal: Count the number of unordered pairs of equal elements in an integer array.
Details: countPairs(int[] arr) iterates over all index pairs (i, j) with i < j and increments the counter when arr[i] == arr[j], returning the total.

mbpp_0403.reference_description: Write a function to check if a url is valid or not using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if a url is valid or not using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: URLValidator
Main goal: Offer a utility to validate HTTP/HTTPS URLs using a regex. It exposes isValidURL(String) which returns true if the input matches the URL pattern and is not null; otherwise false.

mbpp_0095.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum length of sublist.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum length of sublist.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Minimum inner-list length
Goal: Compute and return the smallest number of elements across all sublists in a List<List<?>> by iterating the sublists and tracking the minimum size; does not guard against nulls.

mbpp_0093.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the value of 'a' to the power 'b'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the value of 'a' to the power 'b'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive integer power function
Main goal: Compute a^b for non-negative integers a and b using recursion. Base cases: b == 0 returns 1; a == 0 returns 0 (for b > 0); b == 1 returns a. Otherwise, returns a * power(a, b-1). Note: does not handle negative exponents; 0^0 is treated as 1 by this implementation.

mbpp_0092.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given number is undulating or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given number is undulating or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: UndulatingChecker
Main goal: Check if a string has a two-step repeating (undulating) pattern by verifying that every character equals the one two positions earlier (s[i] == s[i-2] for all i >= 2); returns true for strings longer than 2 that follow this pattern (e.g., "abab", "aaaa", "aba"), and false otherwise.

mbpp_0949.reference_description: Write a function to sort the given tuple array basis the total digits in tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort the given tuple array basis the total digits in tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: TupleSorter sorts a list of lists by the total length of their elements' string representations
Goal: For each inner list, compute the sum of lengths of toString() of its elements, sort the outer list in ascending order by that sum, and return the sorted list as a string.

mbpp_0127.reference_description: Write a function to multiply two integers without using the * operator in java.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to multiply two integers without using the * operator in java.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive multiplication by addition
Main goal: Compute the product of two integers x and y by recursively adding x, handling negative y by negating the result, with base cases for y == 0 (0) and y == 1 (x).

mbpp_0166.reference_description: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an even number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an even number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count pairs with even XOR (same parity)
Main goal: Count the number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j for which A[i] XOR A[j] is even. This occurs when A[i] and A[j] share the same parity (both even or both odd). The method findEvenPair uses a brute-force O(N^2) approach to accumulate and return the count.

mbpp_0167.reference_description: Write a java function to find smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Implement nextPowerOf2(int n) to return the smallest power of two that is greater than or equal to n. If n is already a power of two, it returns n; for n = 0 it returns 1. Note: behavior for negative inputs and for large values (potential overflow near Integer.MAX_VALUE) is undefined/unsafe.

mbpp_0241.reference_description: Write a function to generate a 3d array having each element as '*'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to generate a 3d array having each element as '*'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: 3D String Array Generator
Goal: Create and return a 3D String array with dimensions o x n x m, initializing every element to the string "*".

mbpp_0556.reference_description: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an odd number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the pairs with xor as an odd number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count of Pairs with Odd XOR
Main goal: Given an array A of length N, count how many pairs (i, j) with i < j have A[i] XOR A[j] odd; implemented with a nested loop that increments the count when (A[i] ^ A[j]) % 2 != 0 (i.e., A[i] and A[j] have different parity). Returns the total count (O(N^2) time).

mbpp_0296.reference_description: Write a java function to count inversions in an array.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: InversionCounter - Brute-force inversion count
Goal: Compute the number of inversions in the given array, i.e., the number of pairs (i, j) with i < j and arr[i] > arr[j], using a straightforward O(n^2) nested loop. Returns the total count.

mbpp_0527.reference_description: Write a function to find all pairs in an integer array whose sum is equal to a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all pairs in an integer array whose sum is equal to a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PairSum - Count Pairs with Target Sum
Main goal: Given an array and a target sum, count how many pairs of distinct elements (i < j) add up to the target, using a brute-force O(n^2) approach.

mbpp_0564.reference_description: Write a java function to count unequal element pairs from the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count unequal element pairs from the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PairCounter - Brute-force count of unequal element pairs
Main goal: Given an array and its length n, return the number of index pairs (i, j) with i < j such that arr[i] != arr[j]. Implemented via a nested loop (O(n^2)).

mbpp_0767.reference_description: Write a java function to count the number of pairs whose sum is equal to ‘sum’.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the number of pairs whose sum is equal to ‘sum’.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: PairSumCounter - Counts pairs with a given sum
Main goal: Count how many pairs of elements in the input array sum to the specified value using a brute-force nested loop (i < j), and return the total count.

mbpp_0611.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum of nth column from the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum of nth column from the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Max of Nth Elements Across Sublists
Main goal: Given a List<List<T>> where T is Comparable, find and return the greatest value located at index N among all inner lists by iterating and comparing the Nth element of each sublist. It uses a generic type T with bounds T extends Comparable<? super T>. Assumes all inner lists have at least N+1 elements and that testList is non-empty; otherwise it may throw exceptions.

mbpp_0841.reference_description: Write a function to count the number of inversions in the given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count the number of inversions in the given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: InversionCounter
Main goal: Count the number of inversions in an array by checking all pairs (i, j) with i < j and counting each time arr[i] > arr[j]. The getInvCount method uses a nested loop (brute-force O(n^2)) to return the total inversion count.

mbpp_0849.reference_description: Write a java function to find sum of all prime divisors of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find sum of all prime divisors of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code computes the sum of the distinct prime divisors of N. It uses a sieve-like method: for each i from 2 to N, if i has not been marked yet (sumOfPrimeDivisors[i] == 0), it treats i as prime and adds i to sumOfPrimeDivisors[j] for every multiple j of i up to N. The returned value is the sum of N's unique prime factors (0 for N < 2).

mbpp_0165.reference_description: Write a java function to count characters at same position in a given string (lower and uppercase characters) as in english alphabet.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count characters at same position in a given string (lower and uppercase characters) as in english alphabet.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: CharacterPositionCounter – Counts characters whose alphabet index matches their string position. The method countCharPosition iterates through the string and increments a counter when the zero-based index i equals the character's alphabet index (case-insensitive, where A/a -> 0, B/b -> 1, …).

mbpp_0103.reference_description: Write a function to find eulerian number a(n, m).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find eulerian number a(n, m).
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code implements a recursive computation of Eulerian numbers A(n, m). It defines eulerianNum(n, m) that returns 0 if n is 0 or m ≥ n, returns 1 if m is 0, and otherwise uses the Eulerian recurrence A(n, m) = (n−m)·A(n−1, m−1) + (m+1)·A(n−1, m).

mbpp_0914.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given string is made up of two alternating characters or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given string is made up of two alternating characters or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: AlternatingStringChecker - checks two-character alternating pattern
Main goal: The isTwoAlter method returns true if the input string is composed of exactly two distinct characters that strictly alternate (e.g., "ababab" or "010101"). It does this by ensuring s[i] == s[i+2] for all i in [0, length-3], and by requiring the first two characters to be different. Note: the code will throw an exception for strings of length 0 or 1 due to an unchecked access to s.charAt(1).

mbpp_0291.reference_description: Write a function to find out the number of ways of painting the fence such that at most 2 adjacent posts have the same color for the given fence with n posts and k colors.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find out the number of ways of painting the fence such that at most 2 adjacent posts have the same color for the given fence with n posts and k colors.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Calculates the number of ways to color n fence posts with k colors (mod 1e9+7) so that no color appears on three consecutive posts. It uses DP: dp[1] = k, dp[2] = k^2, and for i ≥ 3, dp[i] = (k−1) · (dp[i−1] + dp[i−2]); returns dp[n].

mbpp_0683.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by sum of two squares or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given number can be represented by sum of two squares or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SumSquareChecker - Brute-force check for a sum of two squares
Main goal: Determine if a given integer n can be written as i^2 + j^2 for positive integers i and j using a brute-force search.
How it works: sumSquare(n) uses two nested loops over i and j starting from 1 up to sqrt(n); if it finds any pair with i^2 + j^2 == n, it returns true; otherwise it returns false after exhausting all pairs.

mbpp_0352.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether all the characters in a given string are unique.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether all the characters in a given string are unique.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: UniqueCharacters - Check for unique characters in a string
Main goal: Determine if all characters in the input string are distinct by comparing each character with all subsequent characters, returning true if no duplicates exist and false otherwise (O(n^2) time).

mbpp_0562.reference_description: Write a java function to find the maximum length of sublist.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the maximum length of sublist.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: MaxLengthFinder - Determine the maximum inner-list size
Main goal: Given a List containing sublists (of any element types), compute and return the largest size among the inner lists by iterating through each sublist and tracking the maximum length. Returns 0 if the outer list is empty or all sublists are empty.

mbpp_0461.reference_description: Write a java function to count the upper case characters in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the upper case characters in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: UpperCounter
Main goal: Count the number of uppercase letters (A–Z) in a given string.
Notes: There is a bug—the return statement is inside the for loop, causing the method to return after evaluating only the first character; it should return after the loop completes.

mbpp_0028.reference_description: Write a java function to find binomial co-efficient.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find binomial co-efficient.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: BinomialCoefficient: Java class that computes C(n, k) recursively (Pascal’s rule) with base cases k>n -> 0 and k==0 or k==n -> 1; but it’s exponential and can overflow int for large n.

mbpp_0764.reference_description: Write a java function to count numeric values in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count numeric values in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Digit Counter in a String
Main goal: Count how many digit characters (0-9) appear in a given string.
What it does: The NumberCounter.numberCtr method iterates over each character in the input string, increments a counter when the character is between '0' and '9', and returns the total count.

mbpp_0803.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given number is a perfect square or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given number is a perfect square or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Perfect Square Checker
Goal: Determine whether an integer n is a perfect square by iterating potential square roots i and returning true if n is divisible by i and n/i equals i; otherwise return false. Time complexity is O(sqrt(n)) with O(1) space. Note: may overflow for large n due to i*i in the loop condition and it treats 0 as not a perfect square; a safer check is i <= n / i.

mbpp_0818.reference_description: Write a java function to count lower case letters in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count lower case letters in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: LowerCounter - Counts lowercase letters in a string
Main goal: Implement a function that returns how many lowercase ASCII letters ('a' to 'z') appear in a given string.
How it works: The lowerCtr method loops through each character of the input string, checks if the character is between 'a' and 'z', increments a counter for each match, and returns the total count.

mbpp_0346.reference_description: Write a function to find entringer number e(n, k).

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find entringer number e(n, k).
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The Zigzag class defines a recursive function zigzag(n, k) that computes a combinatorial count parameterized by n and k. The goal is to evaluate the quantity according to the recurrence: base cases are (n==0 && k==0) -> 1 and (k==0) -> 0 (for n>0); for general n,k it returns zigzag(n, k-1) + zigzag(n-1, n-k). There is no memoization, so the function is exponential in time and can produce invalid calls if k > n (negative indices). The code itself implements the recurrence rather than performing I/O or higher-level logic.

mbpp_0150.reference_description: Write a java function to find whether the given number is present in the infinite sequence or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find whether the given number is present in the infinite sequence or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: SequenceUtils.doesContainB
Main goal: Check if b lies on the arithmetic sequence starting at a with step c (including a). It returns true if a == b, or if b − a is a nonzero multiple of c with the same sign as c (i.e., b = a + n·c for some n ≥ 1); otherwise, it returns false.

mbpp_0126.reference_description: Write a java function to find the sum of common divisors of two given numbers.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the sum of common divisors of two given numbers.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Goal: Compute the sum of all common divisors of two integers a and b by testing each i from 1 up to min(a, b) - 1 and adding i when it divides both numbers.

mbpp_0464.reference_description: Write a function to check if all values are same in map.

mbpp_0334.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the triangle is valid or not if sides are given.

mbpp_0891.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the given two numbers have same number of digits or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the given two numbers have same number of digits or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Purpose: Determine if two integers have the same number of decimal digits by repeatedly dividing both by 10 until one reaches zero, and returning true if both reach zero simultaneously; otherwise false.

mbpp_0923.reference_description: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the length of the shortest string that has both str1 and str2 as subsequences.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Recursive Length Calculator for Shortest Common Supersequence
Main goal: Compute the length of the shortest common supersequence (SCS) of two strings X and Y using a naive recursive approach. The method treats m and n as the current prefix lengths of X and Y. Base cases: if m == 0 return n; if n == 0 return m. If the last characters match (X[m-1] == Y[n-1]), it recurses on (m-1, n-1) and adds 1. Otherwise, it recurses on (m-1, n) and (m, n-1), takes the minimum, and adds 1. The function returns the length of the SCS (not the sequence itself) and is not optimized (no memoization).

mbpp_0521.reference_description: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to print check if the triangle is scalene or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Scalene sides checker
Main goal: Determine whether three integers x, y, z are all pairwise different (x != y, y != z, z != x) and return true if they are; otherwise return false. Note: It does not verify the triangle inequality, i.e., it only checks the distinctness of the sides.

mbpp_0148.reference_description: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to divide a number into two parts such that the sum of digits is maximum.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Digit-sum decomposition via all-9s prefix
Main goal: For a given N, split it into A (the largest number of the form 99...9 not exceeding N) and the remainder N−A, then return the sum of digits of A plus the sum of digits of the remainder. Also includes a helper to sum digits of a number.

Functions:
- sumDigitsSingle(x): returns the sum of decimal digits of x.
- closest(x): returns the largest all-9s number (9, 99, 999, ...) that is <= x (or 0 if x < 9).
- sumDigitsTwoParts(N): computes sumDigitsSingle(A) + sumDigitsSingle(N−A) with A = closest(N).

mbpp_0462.reference_description: Write a function to find all possible combinations of the elements of a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all possible combinations of the elements of a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Power set generator for a list
Main goal: Return all possible subsets (the power set) of the input list as a List<List<T>>. It uses recursion: for the rest of the list, it obtains all subsets, then for each subset it adds two versions to the result—one without the first element and one with the first element—thus generating every combination (including the empty set and the full set). For an empty input, it returns a list containing the empty subset.

mbpp_0630.reference_description: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to extract all the adjacent coordinates of the given coordinate tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: AdjacentCoordinates — enumerate nearby coordinate tuples
Main goal: Given an input int[] testTup, generate all combinations where each element is replaced by its value in {x-1, x, x+1}. The code recursively builds the Cartesian product of these neighborhoods and returns the result as a List<List<Integer>>.

mbpp_0255.reference_description: Write a function to choose specified number of colours from three different colours and generate all the combinations with repetitions.

It builds sequences where each next element is chosen from the current index or later (start = i), allowing repeated elements, and collects each complete combination into the result as a separate list.

mbpp_0348.reference_description: Write a function to count sequences of given length having non-negative prefix sums that can be generated by given values.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count sequences of given length having non-negative prefix sums that can be generated by given values.

mbpp_0259.reference_description: Write a function to maximize the given two tuples.

If one outer or inner list is shorter, the remaining elements are ignored.

mbpp_0540.reference_description: Write a java function to find the difference between highest and least frequencies in a given array.

Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Note: the last group is not processed due to a missing update after the loop (a potential bug).

mbpp_0445.reference_description: Write a function to perform index wise multiplication of tuple elements in the given two tuples.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to perform index wise multiplication of tuple elements in the given two tuples.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Element-wise multiplication of paired rows from two 2D integer lists
Main goal: The function indexMultiplication takes two lists of integer lists (2D lists) and produces a new 2D list. For each row i up to the smaller number of rows between the inputs, it multiplies corresponding elements of the two rows (j up to the smaller row length) and stores those products in a new row. The result has as many rows as the shorter input, and each resulting row has a length equal to the shorter length of the paired input rows.

mbpp_0598.reference_description: Write a function to check whether the given number is armstrong or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check whether the given number is armstrong or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Armstrong Number Checker
Goal: Determine if a number is an Armstrong (narcissistic) number by counting its digits, summing each digit raised to that power, and returning true if the sum equals the original number.

mbpp_0631.reference_description: Write a function to replace whitespaces with an underscore and vice versa in a given string by using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to replace whitespaces with an underscore and vice versa in a given string by using regex.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: ReplaceSpaces
Main goal: Swap spaces and underscores in a string (spaces become underscores and underscores become spaces) using a regex [ _] and the Matcher.appendReplacement approach, leaving all other characters untouched.

mbpp_0844.reference_description: Write a java function to find the kth element in an array containing odd elements first and then even elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the kth element in an array containing odd elements first and then even elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Construct an array containing the numbers from 1 to n with all odd numbers first (ascending), followed by all even numbers (ascending), and return the k-th element (1-based) of that sequence.

mbpp_0289.reference_description: Write a java function to calculate the number of odd days in a given year.

mbpp_0709.reference_description: Write a function to count unique keys for each value present in the tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count unique keys for each value present in the tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Count unique keys per value in a list of key-value pairs
Main goal: Given a list of SimpleEntry<K, V>, return a map from each distinct value V to the number of distinct keys K that map to that value (i.e., the count of unique keys for each value).

mbpp_0005.reference_description: Write a function to find the number of ways to fill it with 2 x 1 dominoes for the given 3 x n board.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the number of ways to fill it with 2 x 1 dominoes for the given 3 x n board.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
The code uses two-state dynamic programming to count tilings of a 2 x n structure (or a similar sequential arrangement) with specific tiles. It maintains two arrays, A and B:
- A[i] = number of complete tilings up to length i.
- B[i] = number of tilings ending with a single exposed cell at position i (an incomplete/partial tiling).

Initialization: A[0] = 1, A[1] = 0, B[0] = 0, B[1] = 1 (if n >= 1).

Transition:
- A[i] = A[i - 2] + 2 * B[i - 1]
- B[i] = A[i - 1] + B[i - 2]

The function returns A[n]. This yields zero for odd n and nonzero values for even n (e.g., A[2] = 3, A[4] = 11, A[6] = 41, …).

mbpp_0045.reference_description: Write a function to find the gcd of the given array elements.

mbpp_0645.reference_description: Write a function to find the product of it’s kth index in the given tuples.

mbpp_0057.reference_description: Write a java function to find the largest number that can be formed with the given digits.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the largest number that can be formed with the given digits.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Implementation notes: it converts the primitive int[] to Integer[] to use Collections.reverseOrder with Arrays.sort, then iteratively appends digits by starting with the first (largest) digit and for each remaining digit multiplying the current value by 10 and adding the next digit. Assumes all elements are digits 0–9; for multi-digit elements the logic would not produce a standard decimal concatenation.

mbpp_0823.reference_description: Write a function to check if the given string starts with a substring using regex.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to check if the given string starts with a substring using regex.

mbpp_0164.reference_description: Write a java function to check whether the sum of divisors are same or not.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to check whether the sum of divisors are same or not.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:

Main goal: Provide utilities to compute the sum of divisors of a number and compare two numbers by that sum.
Functions:
- divSum(n): initializes sum to 1, iterates i from 2 to floor(sqrt(n)); if n % i == 0, adds i and n/i. Returns sum. Note: does not include n itself; for perfect squares it double-counts the square root.
- areEquivalent(num1, num2): returns true if divSum(num1) == divSum(num2).

mbpp_0114.reference_description: Write a function to assign frequency to each tuple in the given tuple array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to assign frequency to each tuple in the given tuple array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Given a list of integer lists, the code counts how many times each inner list occurs (treating lists with identical elements as the same key) using a LinkedHashMap to preserve the order of first appearance. It then builds a new list where each unique inner list is copied and augmented with its frequency as the last element, and returns this as a string. In short: it maps each sublist to its frequency and outputs the sublists with their counts in input order.

mbpp_0658.reference_description: Write a function to find the item with maximum occurrences in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the item with maximum occurrences in a given array.

Notes: time complexity is O(n^2); assumes a non-empty list (will fail on empty), and in case of ties it returns the first encountered item with the maximum frequency.

mbpp_0220.reference_description: Write a function to replace maximum n occurrences of spaces, commas, or dots with a colon.

Description_Simple.comparison_text: Replaces up to n occurrences of spaces, commas, or periods in the input text with a colon, using a regex to locate matches and a StringBuffer to build the result.

mbpp_0662.reference_description: Write a function to sort array in map.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to sort array in map.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Creates and returns a new map with the same keys as the input, but with each value being a sorted copy of the original List<V> (V must be Comparable). It iterates entries, copies and sorts each list, and stores it in a new map, leaving the original map unchanged.

mbpp_0217.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first repeated character in a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the first repeated character in a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: First Repeated Character Finder
Main goal: Find and return the first repeated character in a string (left-to-right); uses a HashSet to track seen characters; returns '\0' if none repeats.

mbpp_0895.reference_description: Write a function to find the maximum sum of subsequences of given array with no adjacent elements.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find the maximum sum of subsequences of given array with no adjacent elements.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Maximum Sum Subsequence with No Adjacent Elements (Dynamic Programming)

Main goal: Given an integer array, compute the largest possible sum by selecting a subsequence with no two chosen elements adjacent. It uses a DP array where lookUp[i] stores the best sum up to index i: initialize lookUp[0] = A[0], lookUp[1] = max(A[0], A[1]); for i ≥ 2, lookUp[i] = max(lookUp[i-1], lookUp[i-2] + A[i], A[i]). Returns lookUp[n-1]. Time complexity: O(n); Space complexity: O(n).

mbpp_0958.reference_description: Write a function to convert an integer into a roman numeral.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to convert an integer into a roman numeral.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Integer to Roman Numeral Converter
Main goal: Convert a positive integer to its Roman numeral representation by greedily mapping standard Roman numerals. The intToRoman method uses parallel arrays of values and symbols, repeatedly subtracting the largest possible value and appending the corresponding symbol to a StringBuilder until the input number reaches zero.

mbpp_0707.reference_description: Write a java function to count the total set bits from 1 to n.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to count the total set bits from 1 to n.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Summary_description:
Title: Total set bits in numbers from 0 to n
Main goal: Compute the total number of set bits (ones) in binary representations of all integers from 0 up to n (inclusive). The method countSetBits(n) performs an efficient per-bit calculation by iterating over powers of two, summing contributions from full blocks and a possible remainder, returning the total as a long. Time complexity is O(log n).

mbpp_0786.reference_description: Write a function to locate the right insertion point for a specified value in sorted order.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to locate the right insertion point for a specified value in sorted order.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: RightInsertion - upper bound index in a sorted list
Main goal: Given a sorted List<T> (T extends Comparable<? super T>), return the insertion index for x that keeps the list sorted — specifically the first index after the last element ≤ x (the upper bound). Implemented via a binary search, runs in O(log n) and does not modify the list.

mbpp_0169.reference_description: Write a function to calculate the nth pell number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to calculate the nth pell number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: PellCalculator computes the nth Pell number using an iterative recurrence. It returns P(n) with P(0)=0, P(1)=1, P(2)=2 and P(n)=2*P(n-1)+P(n-2) for n≥3, implemented in O(n) time and O(1) extra space (using long).

mbpp_0200.reference_description: Write a function to find all index positions of the maximum values in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all index positions of the maximum values in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Locate All Indices of the Maximum in a List
Goal: For a list of integers, determine the maximum value and return a list of all indices where that maximum value occurs.

mbpp_0155.reference_description: Write a java function to toggle all even bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to toggle all even bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Toggle odd-position bits in an integer
Main goal: Create a mask with 1s at all odd bit positions (1,3,5,...) up to the most significant bit of n, and return n XOR mask, effectively flipping those bits of n while leaving even-position bits unchanged.

mbpp_0048.reference_description: Write a java function to set all odd bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to set all odd bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: OddBitSetNumber - set even-position bits up to MSB
Main goal: Build a mask with 1s at even bit indices (0, 2, 4, ...) up to the most significant bit of n, then return n OR mask. This results in turning on all even-positioned bits up to the MSB while preserving the original odd bits.

mbpp_0235.reference_description: Write a java function to set all even bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to set all even bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: evenBitSetNumber - Set all odd-positioned bits up to the MSB of n
Main goal: Return n OR a mask that has 1s at all odd bit indices (1, 3, 5, ...) from the least significant bit up to the most significant set bit of n. This forces all odd bits in that range to 1 while preserving the original even bits.
How it works: It walks through the bits of n, builds a mask (res) with 1s at odd positions, and returns n | res.

mbpp_0246.reference_description: Write a function for computing square roots using the babylonian method.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function for computing square roots using the babylonian method.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Implements the Babylonian (Heron's/Newton-Raphson) method to compute the square root of a non-negative number. It initializes the guess to number/2 and iteratively refines g with g = (g + number/g)/2 until convergence, returning 0 when the input is 0.

mbpp_0305.reference_description: Write a function to match two words from array of words starting with letter 'p'.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to match two words from array of words starting with letter 'p'.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: Title: WordMatcher - Find two P-prefixed words at the start of a string. Main goal: Iterate over a list of strings and return the first two words that start with 'P' (captured as group 1 and group 2) separated by a non-word character, or null if none are found.

mbpp_0218.reference_description: Write a java function to find the minimum operations required to make two numbers equal.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to find the minimum operations required to make two numbers equal.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: The code defines a helper that computes a specific integer from two positive integers A and B: it ensures A <= B, computes g = gcd(A,B) via the Euclidean algorithm, then replaces B by B/g and returns B/g - 1. In effect, the result depends only on the reduced value of B after removing their greatest common divisor with A, and the gcd method implements the standard Euclidean algorithm. The overall complexity is O(log min(A,B)).

mbpp_0322.reference_description: Write a function to find all index positions of the minimum values in a given array.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to find all index positions of the minimum values in a given array.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Find indices of the minimum value in a list
Main goal: Given a list of integers, identify the smallest value and return a list of all indices where that minimum value occurs.
Function details: positionMin computes the minimum with Collections.min and then collects all positions i where list1.get(i) equals that minimum, returning the list of these indices.

mbpp_0363.reference_description: Write a function to add the k elements to each element in the tuple.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to add the k elements to each element in the tuple.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: Increment each element by K in a 2D list
Main goal: Return a new List<List<Integer>> where every integer in the input testList is increased by K.
How: For each sublist, create a new sublist, add (element + K) for each element, and collect into the result.

mbpp_0332.reference_description: Write a function to count character frequency of a given string.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a function to count character frequency of a given string.
Description_Simple.comparison_text: FrequencyCounter.charFrequency builds a frequency map of characters in the given string by iterating all characters and counting occurrences in a HashMap, returning a Map<Character,Integer> of character counts.

mbpp_0383.reference_description: Write a java function to toggle all odd bits of a given number.

Description_Simple.reference_text: Write a java function to toggle all odd bits of a given number.
Description_Simple.comparison_text:
Title: evenBitToggleNumber flips even-position bits
Main goal: Given an int n, construct a mask with 1s at even bit positions (0,2,4,…) up to the most significant bit, then return n XOR mask to toggle those bits (unchanged for negative inputs).

mbpp_0537.reference_description: Write a java function to find the first repeated word in a given string.
